design.estimand: Causal effect of the magnitude of offensive reorganization relative to lineup L on the change in points per possession for the team in games with a player absence spell.
design.unit: Game-level difference (pre‑absence vs post‑absence) or possession-level transition from before to after absence.
design.sample: All 986 games with a documented player absence, but only those where the absence lasted ≥20 minutes and involved at least one core offensive player. This yields ~350–400 games for analysis.
design.power: Assuming a moderate effect size (Cohen's d≈0.4) and α=0.05, the sample provides ~70% power. We will perform a post‑hoc power analysis using the observed variance of points per possession changes.
design.controls: Lineup quality (team offensive rating, average player PER), opponent defensive rating, game tempo (possessions per game), home/away indicator, rest days, and period of the game (first vs second half). Fixed effects for team and opponent will be included.
design.falsification: Apply the same model to a shuffled reorganization metric (randomly permuted across games) to test for spurious correlations. Additionally, test the model on games without absences to ensure no systematic bias.
design.multiplicity: Pre‑register a single primary hypothesis test; secondary exploratory analyses will be clearly labeled.
design.decision_rule: If the estimated coefficient on reorganization magnitude is statistically significant (p<0.05) and the effect size exceeds a pre‑defined threshold (Δ>0.02 points per possession), conclude support. If the coefficient is non‑significant and the confidence interval includes zero, conclude rejection. If power is insufficient or model diagnostics fail, label the result as untestable.
